# mbse-patterns

> Predicates, queries and (planned) patterns over mbse-schemas data, with mbse-expressions' rules. A predicate is a named Basic rule over symbols, each bound to an object of a schema, kept as data beside the schemas and built fluently, as schemas are; it applies to matches, combinations of objects. Validators check data against predicates, three-valued (unknown is not false), and queries find a store's matches, streaming lazily, planned from the rule's shape (early tests, hops through relations, `unique` clauses), through a queryable-store protocol with an in-memory implementation over any store. Equivalent Python (`mbse.Patterns`) and TypeScript (`@mbse/patterns`) implementations write byte-identical JSON.

Patterns (weights over predicates, with distributions of properties and relations), byte-identical pseudorandom generators and streaming characterizers are designed for the next releases.

## Using it

- [Agent skill](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-patterns/blob/main/skills/mbse-patterns/SKILL.md): when to use it, the rules that prevent most mistakes, and references loaded per task
- [Python](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-patterns/blob/main/skills/mbse-patterns/references/python.md) and [TypeScript](https://github.com/pitaman71/mbse-patterns/blob/main/skills/mbse-patterns/references/typescript.md): a complete program, cheat sheet and traps
